$comment: Generated by semantius 0.8.37 (generate_module_schema); transfer file version 1.
title: Semantius transfer file
description: One JSON document written by export_entities / export_module and read by import_entities / import_module. Metadata is keyed by names, never by host ids: the module by module_name, roles by slug, permissions by permission_name. This schema describes what this CLI writes and reads. A column outside it is dropped by the import (so it is flagged here); it says nothing about what a given host accepts. Layout: the CLI writes metadata pretty-printed and each record as one compact line inside its entity's "records" block, which lets the import stream a large file. A file reformatted by hand still imports, but is parsed whole.

$schema.description: Optional: point an editor at this schema. The import ignores it.

version.description: Format version; this CLI reads 1 only.

module_type.description: Module type: domain (normal, the default) or master (promoted for sharing); any other value is rejected. Normally set when the module is created. Create-only: sent when the row is created on the target, never changed by a later import.

view_permission.description: Permission required to view this module, by name. It must already exist when the module is created: this is a foreign key, and each request is its own transaction, so a permission created by a later request is too late. Create the module with an existing permission (the default "user:read" works), then create the module's own permissions, then update the module.

manage_permission.description: Manage permission of this module, by name. A foreign key: the permission must already exist.

admin_permission.description: Admin permission of this module, by name. A foreign key: the permission must already exist.

default_viewer_role_slug.description: slug of the role named by default_viewer_role_id on the exporting host (a role of this module, or of another module that must exist on the target); null for none

default_manager_role_slug.description: slug of the role named by default_manager_role_id on the exporting host (a role of this module, or of another module that must exist on the target); null for none

default_admin_role_slug.description: slug of the role named by default_admin_role_id on the exporting host (a role of this module, or of another module that must exist on the target); null for none

logo_color.description: Hex color code for module logo, lowercase (for example #4f46e5)

icon_name.description: Icon shown for the module: a Lucide icon name in kebab-case (e.g. "users"; latest Lucide release, names searchable in https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lucide-static/tags.json) or an icon URL

home_page.description: Default home page path for module

module_slug.description: URL-safe unique identifier for the module: lowercase, starting with a letter or digit, using only a-z, 0-9, - and _. Derived from the module name when left empty.

dashboard_config.description: Layout and widgets of the module dashboard (JSON)

catalog_module_code.description: Catalog blueprint this module was provisioned/cloned from; also the domain axis (non-unique). Write-once: set on create or filled once while empty, then never changed. Empty = not generated from a catalog spec. Create-only: sent when the row is created on the target, never changed by a later import.

domain_code.description: Short uppercase code for the business domain this module belongs to (e.g. ATS, HCM, ITSM, CRM).

access_scope.description: Permission structure of the module. Omitted, it is custom. custom: custom permission structure. basic: two permissions, view and edit. advanced: three permissions, view, edit and admin. gated: view, edit and admin, plus a permission per process gate held by admins. raci: view, edit and admin, plus a permission per process gate held by RACI roles (and by admins, except for high-risk gates).

module.description: The module itself. Present in a file from export_module, absent from export_entities; import_module needs it.

permission_name.description: The permission itself, and the key other tables use to name it. Colon-separated segments of a-z, 0-9, - and _, each starting with a letter or digit, e.g. crm:read or service-catalog:view. No spaces, commas or dots: scope strings are split on commas and whitespace, and a dot would make permission_hierarchy ids ambiguous.

permission_hierarchy.description: Hierarchy rows that touch the module's permissions, from either side; the other side must exist on the target (module file only).

including_permission_name.description: The broader permission, by name: holding it implies the included permission (e.g. crm:manage includes crm:read).

included_permission_name.description: The narrower permission that is included by the broader one, by name (e.g. "crm:read" in "crm:manage includes crm:read").

origin.description: How the hierarchy entry was created: system (reserved for the platform), model (declared in the model of a domain module), model_master (created by the deployer for a master module, inside it or between it and other modules) or user (added by an admin). Set on insert and never changed. Defaults to user when omitted.

slug.description: Snake_case unique identifier for the role, derived from role_name when omitted. Cannot be changed on a system role. Create-only: sent when the row is created on the target, never changed by a later import.

origin.description: How the role was created: system (platform built-in), model (scaffold role of a domain module), model_master (scaffold role of a master module) or user (created by an admin). Set on insert and never changed. Defaults to user when omitted. Create-only: sent when the row is created on the target, never changed by a later import.

catalog_role_code.description: Stable catalog persona/role this role was provisioned from (lineage; non-unique). Write-once: set on create or filled once while empty, then never changed. Empty = not generated from a catalog spec.

role_permissions.description: Grants of the roles above (module file only).

items.description: A role holding a permission, both by name.

role_slug.description: slug of a role in this file

entity.description: The entity definition. With exclude_schema the export carries table_name alone; any other entry carries its fields and the required columns.

table_name.description: Physical table name: lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter or _, and not ending in _ext (reserved). Primary key. Changing it on update renames the physical table.

singular.description: Singular form of table name (on create, auto-derived from table_name when blank)

plural.description: Plural form of table name, auto-assigned to table_name

singular_label.description: Human-readable singular noun for UI/reports (e.g. Customer), symmetric with plural_label. On create, when blank it is derived from label_column (service_name becomes "Service Name"), so pass it. It does not set the title of the label field, which is always "Name".

plural_label.description: Human-readable plural label for UI/reports (e.g. Customers)

icon_name.description: Icon shown for the entity: a Lucide icon name in kebab-case (e.g. "users"; latest Lucide release, names searchable in https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lucide-static/tags.json) or an icon URL

name_sort.description: Sort key that orders entities in navigation

module_name.description: module_name of the module the entity belongs to

view_permission.description: Permission required to SELECT from this table, by name. It must already exist: this is a foreign key to permissions(permission_name), so an unregistered name is rejected with a foreign-key error rather than accepted. Create the permission first, then the entity. A rollup between two entities with different view permissions needs include_hidden_rows (90269).

edit_permission.description: Permission required to INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE from this table, by name. Same foreign key as view_permission: the permission must already exist. A permission an entity names cannot be deleted while the entity stands.

id_column.description: Name of the primary key column (default id), created automatically. Set on create and locked afterwards (a change is refused with 90253); omit it on update. Create-only: sent when the row is created on the target, never changed by a later import.

id_type.description: Key type of the table, set on create and locked afterwards (changing it is refused with 90233); omit it on update. auto_increment (the default when omitted): a 64-bit number the database assigns. bigint: a 64-bit number the caller supplies on every insert. text: a text key the caller supplies. uuid: a time-ordered UUIDv7 the database assigns. typeid: a prefixed, sortable TypeID such as acct_01h455vb4pex5vsknk084sn02q, assigned by the database; requires id_prefix. is_a: a subtype of the typeid or is_a entity named in id_refentity; each record is exactly one type, shares the key of its base record and carries the subtype's own prefix; requires id_prefix and id_refentity. has_a: an optional extension of the typeid entity named in id_refentity; a base record has at most one, and it takes the base record's key; requires id_refentity. computed: system tables only, refused for a new entity (90234). The id field itself is created automatically; never create it with create_field. is_a and has_a entities cannot set label_column, label_parent or order_column. Create-only: sent when the row is created on the target, never changed by a later import.

id_prefix.description: TypeID prefix, required when id_type is typeid or is_a and empty otherwise: up to 63 lowercase letters and underscores, starting and ending with a letter (e.g. acct). Unique among entities. A typeid entity may change it later: new ids take the new prefix, existing ids keep theirs, and an id with a former prefix can no longer be inserted. An is_a entity keeps the prefix it was created with (90245), because the prefix is what says which subtype a record is.

id_refentity.description: The entity an is_a or has_a entity is based on, whose key its records share. An is_a entity is based on a typeid or is_a entity, a has_a entity on a typeid entity. Set when the entity is created and never changed; empty for every other key type. Omit it on update (a change is refused with 90241). Create-only: sent when the row is created on the target, never changed by a later import.

label_column.description: Name of the label/display column, created automatically

label_parent.description: Reference or parent field of this entity whose record label the composed _label is built from (the identity spine). Empty = self-identifying: the composed label is the local label. Not allowed on a junction entity, and the spine must stay acyclic. Changing it re-points the composed label; no data is migrated.

order_column.description: Name of an integer column that stores a fixed row order. Setting it creates an INTEGER NOT NULL column (default 0) on a managed entity, and a record inserted with no value or 0 gets MAX + 10 (10 for the first). Renaming or clearing it drops the old column and its data. Not available for is_a or has_a entities (90249). Empty = no fixed order.

managed.description: When false, automatic DDL execution for table and field changes is disabled

edit_mode.description: UI edit mode for records of this table: auto, sidebar, modal, or page

cube_mode.description: Cube mode for OLAP cube generation. Default auto.

audit_log.description: When TRUE, DML operations on this table are logged to audit_record_logs

computed_fields.description: Ordered list of {name, jsonlogic, description?} entries (name and jsonlogic are required), evaluated and stored on every insert and update: each entry derives the named field from the same record before the write. Saving applies the rules to existing records, and a record that cannot take its new value refuses the save (90908). A named field gets ctype computed, and input_type default or readonly becomes disabled. A rule cannot name a rollup field (90907). Default []. On update the list replaces the stored list: send the full list; [] removes the rules.

validation_rules.description: Ordered list of {code, message, jsonlogic, hint?, description?} entries. code, message and jsonlogic are required; code must be a five-digit class 99 code such as "99001" (otherwise refused with 90905). Each rule must evaluate truthy for the write to succeed. Default []. On update the list replaces the stored list: send the full list; [] removes the rules.

select_rule.description: JsonLogic rule evaluated per row for the FOR SELECT RLS policy: true = the current user may see the record. Empty = no per-row rule. Setting a rule on an entity that a rollup aggregates over needs include_hidden_rows on that rollup (90269).

entity_type.description: What kind of data this entity holds. operational_workflow: records move through a gated lifecycle (even one gated step such as draft to submitted counts). operational_record: everyday business records without such a lifecycle. catalog: reference or lookup data maintained by admins. junction: a pure connecting record between entities with no fields of its own; the platform labels its rows by the records they relate. computed: every field is derived and never written directly. unclassified: not classified yet (the default). Set it on create or change it on update like any other column.

catalog_entity_code.description: Stable canonical identity this entity realizes (domain-map code, e.g. "vendors"); the rename/dialect/silo join key. table_name holds the deployed name. Write-once: set on create or filled once while empty, then never changed. Empty = not generated from a catalog spec. Create-only: sent when the row is created on the target, never changed by a later import.

catalog_owner_module.description: For an embedded-master placeholder, the slug of the module that should own this entity. Soft pointer (not an FK); empty when this module is the owner or the entity is local.

catalog_entity_aliases.description: Reuse/merge record: JSON array of {alias_code, source_domain, source_module, decided}. Append-only. Empty array = never a merge target. Create-only: sent when the row is created on the target, never changed by a later import.

fields.description: The entity's fields in field_order. Absent from an export made with exclude_schema, which carries table_name only.

field_name.description: Physical column name in database: lowercase letters, digits and _. Names starting with _ are reserved for generated system columns such as _label.

title.description: Human-readable display name for the field

description.description: What the field represents. Also written into the column comment, which PostgREST shows in its OpenAPI output.

format.description: JSON Schema format or primitive type. May change only to a format with the same column type (for example text to multiline). A change that would alter the column type is refused (90223; drop and recreate the field instead); the format of a core column cannot change at all (90219).

is_pk.description: Whether this field is the primary key; cannot change after the field is created

default_value.description: Column default, stored as text: a literal value, or one of a fixed list of argument-less SQL expressions (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_DATE, now(), gen_random_uuid(), ...). Any other text is stored as a literal, not evaluated. Maximum 200 characters; no ";", "--" or "/*". Empty means the type's zero value (reference, date and date-time: no default). A number, boolean or JSON value is converted ("1", "true", "{}"). For an enum field give the stored value, never the label.

field_order.description: Display order of the field within its entity

input_type.description: How the UI presents the field for input; input_type_rule can override it per record. On a required field with no input_type_rule, the database also refuses a missing value (90258), except for number and boolean formats, the key, parent fields and a field with an input_type_rule; making a field required while rows lack a value is refused (90259). On a rollup or computed field, default and readonly become disabled, so a form does not submit the derived value.

width.description: Display width of the field in the UI: default (automatic), s (small), m (medium) or w (wide)

ctype.description: Special column type: id, label, audit and core mark a column the dictionary protects; rollup marks a field whose value the database aggregates from its rollup definition, computed a field whose value one of the entity's computed_fields rules writes (the label column keeps label). Derived, never set by hand. Empty is a normal user field, audit covers record-versioning columns such as created_at and updated_at, and core other system columns. A protected column cannot be deleted or renamed (the label column may be renamed), and its format and default value cannot change (the label column's default value may). A rollup or computed field can still be renamed and deleted. Ignored on create; changing it on update is refused with 90214. Read-only: exported for information, never written by the import.

searchable.description: Whether the field is included in full-text search. Takes effect for text-like formats only (not numbers, booleans, JSON or references).

enum_values.description: JSON array in display order. Each entry is a value or a {"value", "label"} object with an optional "description", "color" and "icon", e.g. ["active", {"value": "on_hold", "label": "On hold", "color": "amber"}]. Records store the value; the label, description, color and icon are display hints. color takes an HTML color and icon a Lucide icon name in kebab-case (e.g. "circle-check"; latest Lucide release, names searchable in https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lucide-static/tags.json), as the color and icon formats do. Use an object when the value is a code or abbreviation or needs a color or icon. An empty or missing list means no value check. Unless the field is required, "" is also allowed and is the default. Removing a value still in use is refused (23514).

reference_table.description: Entity this field references, by table name. Required for reference and parent fields, empty for all others, and must name an existing entity.

reference_delete_mode.description: What happens to this record when the referenced record is deleted: restrict (the delete is blocked; the default when omitted, on every format), clear (this field is set to NULL) or cascade (this record is deleted too; refused on a field of an is_a entity, 90249). Only reference and parent fields use it; elsewhere it is ignored. A required reference cannot use clear (90257).

relationship_label.description: Verb describing what the referenced entity does to/with this entity (e.g. "employs", "heads"). Used for ER diagram and navigation labels.

singular_label_parent.description: Custom singular label for the parent entity when format is parent; overrides the singular_label of the parent entity when set

plural_label_parent.description: Custom plural label for the parent entity when format is parent; overrides the plural_label of the parent entity when set

precision.description: Decimal scale of the NUMERIC(18, n) column for format number (0-18, default 2); other formats ignore it. Applied when the column is created; changing it later does not alter the existing column.

unique_value.description: When TRUE, enforces a partial unique index on this column. For string types, NULL and empty string values are excluded from the uniqueness check.

cube_type.description: Role of the field in the generated OLAP cube (dimension or measure); auto lets the platform choose, disabled leaves the field out

input_type_rule.description: JsonLogic rule evaluated client-side against the record being edited. It returns an input_type (default, required, readonly, disabled or hidden) that replaces the static input_type. Empty = no rule.

catalog_field_code.description: Stable design-time field identity (blueprint field name, e.g. "status"); the field-rename join key. Write-once: set on create or filled once while empty, then never changed. Empty = not generated from a catalog spec. Create-only: sent when the row is created on the target, never changed by a later import.

rollup.description: Rollup definition, empty for an ordinary field. Keys: link_field (<child entity>.<reference or parent field pointing at this entity>), function (sum, min, max, avg or count), value_field (a field of the child; not with count), filter (JsonLogic over the child record, restricted to and, or, !, comparisons, in and var; optional) and include_hidden_rows (true accepts aggregating child records that readers of this entity may not see). The field keeps an ordinary format that fits the result: int64 (or int32, integer, number) for count, the value field's own format for min and max, number, integer, int32, int64, float, double or rating for sum, number, float or double for avg (90268 if the format does not fit); precision is copied from the value field when that is a number field. The database maintains the column and sets ctype to rollup. The child entity, link_field and value_field must already exist. A rollup cannot be required, searchable or unique_value (90261), and neither side can be an is_a or has_a entity (90249). Send {} to remove the definition: the field stays, with its last values as ordinary data.

records.description: The records, absent from an export made with exclude_data. The id column is included. Each key is a field_name of the entity; a reference to a user is {"external_id": "..."}, any other reference the id of the referenced row.
